1. The present appeal is filed by the original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 01.08.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi),

sentences.text: Gondal
in MACP No.389 of 2003.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3330/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined 2.

Vide the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the present appellants - original claimants under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present appellants-original claimants entitled to an amount of Rs.5,08,598/- with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.
Thus, the Tribunal has not entertained the claim petition for an amount of Rs.10 lakhs as total compensation.

3. The brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1 On 20.09.2003, the deceased Hirjibhai was working as a Mantri/Secretary in the Milk Producers Cooperative Society of Charkhadi village of Gondal taluka and to get his office computer repaired, he was coming to Rajkot with his office employee,
namely Vijay Hirani on Bajaj-80 motorcycle No. GJ- 3HH-9098 and the deceased was driving that vehicle and Vijay Hirani was sitting behind and he was driving his vehicle peacefully on his side and when he reached near the Bavisi Way Bridge in Rajkot city, the driver of truck bearing No. DL- 1GB-0440 in his charge drove at high speed,
recklessly and in a manner that endangered human life, hit the motorcycle of Hirjibhai, due to which both had fallen down and caused serious injuries to both of them.
3.2

entities.text: Milk Producers Cooperative Society of Charkhadi village of Gondal taluka
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After that, they were rushed to Madhuram Hospital in Rajkot from the spot but due to serious injuries, Hirjibhai died after about four-five hours of treatment and his P.M. has been done in the Government Hospital in Rajkot.

The Accident was caused by the careless driving of the truck driver and a NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3330/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined complaint was registered in Bhaktinagar Police Station, Rajkot City.

At the time of the accident, the deceased husband was 43 years old and was working as a Mantri/Secretary in Shri Charkhadi Milk Producers Cooperative Society and was earning a monthly salary of Rs. 4,500/-.

3.3 Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased being the appellants - original claimants had filed the claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with cost and interest against the respondents before the Tribunal.
3.4 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.
4. This Court vide order dated 29.11.2013 noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants - original claimants and the grounds raised in the appeal, has admitted the appeal.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr. Tushar L. Sheth, learned advocate appearing for the appellants-original claimants has assailed the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal mainly on two counts on the issue of negligency and quantum of compensation.

5.1 Firstly, learned advocate for the appellants - claimants has drawn the attention of this Court to the deduction attributed to the negligence of the deceased, which was considered to the extent of 20% by the learned Tribunal.

It is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3330/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
06/08/2025 undefined submitted that the Tribunal has erred in considering the negligency of 20%
of the deceased.
That, the Insurance company has not examined the Driver of the truck to prove the negligence of the deceased.

So far as the assessment of the income of the deceased is concerned, it is submitted by the learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants that the deceased was earning Rs.4,750/- by working as Mantri/Secretary of Shri Charkhadi Doodh Utpadak Sahakari Mandli.

It is also submitted that the same has been supported by the deposition of one Vijaybhai Ravjibhai Savaliya working in the said Mandli at Exhibit-30 and the evidence produced (being salary sheet Exhibit-31).
However, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased to Rs.2,700/- per month only.

5.2 It is contended that the Tribunal has not properly assessed the income of the deceased/injured,
and has overlooked the settled principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in relation to the assessment of future prospects, application of appropriate multiplier, and grant of compensation under conventional heads such as loss of consortium, loss of estate, and funeral expenses.

It is further submitted that the Tribunal has awarded a meager and unrealistic amount under various heads without considering the financial dependency of the family members and the socio-economic background of the deceased/injured.

The learned counsel has urged that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable, and is liable to be enhanced in accordance with the settled legal principles governing the law of compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3330/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined 6.

Learned advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati appearing of the respondent No.3- Insurance Company has placed reliance upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and vehemently argued that the compensation must be awarded as just, proper and reasonable and not higher side and further submitted that learned Tribunal, after appreciating the materials available on record,
awarded the compensation under each head is just, proper and reasonable and not required to interfere and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.

7. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and perused the record and proceedings and impugned judgment and award, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of negligency.

sentences.text: As regards the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants on the assessment of negligency is concerned, considering the facts of the panchnama and type of the vehicle, it is an indisputable fact that the deceased was on Bajaj M80 Two-wheeler and offending vehicle was a Truck, the learned Tribunal failed to appreciate the fact of type of vehicle.

It also appears from the record that the driver of the offending vehicle did not step into the witness-box and who is the best person to throw the light on the facts of the vehicular accident, and in absence of the evidence of the driver of the offending vehicle, the adverse inference must be drawn on the point of negligence, and therefore, the learned Tribunal failed to appreciate the above important facts and recorded the findings on point of negligence that the deceased was also 20% negligent in the said vehicular accident, which is required NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3330/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
06/08/2025 undefined to be interfered with in the interest of justice.

Under these circumstances,
the opponent - driver of the offending vehicle is held to be 100% negligent in the said accident.

9. As regards the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants on the assessment of the income of the deceased is concerned, the Tribunal has committed error in considering the income of the deceased to the extent of Rs.2,700/- per month only.
It is submitted by the learned advocate for the appellants-original claimants that the deceased was earning Rs.4,750/- by working as Mantri/Secretary of Shri Charkhadi Doodh Utpadak Sahakari Mandli.

It is also submitted that the same has been supported by the deposition of one Vijaybhai Ravjibhai Savaliya working in the said Mandli at Exhibit-30, who stated that the deceased would have got 10% rise on each financial year and the evidence produced (being salary sheet Exhibit-31).
However, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased to Rs.2,700/- per month only and has also erred in considering the future prospective income as Rs. 3,510 with 30% addition.
In that regard, this Court is inclined to enhance the income in view of the aforesaid.
Therefore, the amount awarded under the conventional heads are required to be revised by considering the income of the deceased as Rs.4,750/- per month.

10. As rightly recorded by the Tribunal, considering the fact that the deceased was survived by widow, two children and mother, 1/4th deduction has been applied towards spend by the deceased on himself.

Thus, the calculation of the prospective income of the deceased at the rate of 30% is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/3330/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined considered as Rs.4750/- * 30% (Rs.1425/-) = Rs.6175/-.
After 1/4th deduction towards personal expense of the deceased, the calculation of the income the deceased is Rs.4631/- (Rs.6147/- - Rs.1544/- (1/4th deduction towards personal expenses.)

Noticing the fact that the deceased was aged 48 years at the time of accident, in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and the schedule prescribed, the Tribunal has rightly applied multiplier of 13 in the facts of the case.
